questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

33, 10, 43, 53, 96, ?
questions.solution:

43 + 53 = 96

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd number pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
Out of the given options, 4 - 36 is odd one because in all other options 2ⁿd term is the multiple of 1st term and one exceeding the 1st term i.e.

9 - 90 → 9 × (9 + 1) = 9 × 10 = 90

6 - 42 → 6 × (6 + 1) = 6 × 7 = 42

5 - 30 → 5 × (5 + 1) = 5 × 6 = 30

But in 4 - 36, 4 × (4 + 1) = 4 × 5 = 20 which is not equal to 36.

Thus, 4 - 36 is odd one.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd number pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is that the 2ⁿd number is one more than the cube of first number in each pair except in 5 - 124 i.e.

3 - 28 → 3³ + 1 =27 + 1 = 28

2 - 9 → 2³ + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9

4 - 65 → 4³ + 1 = 64 + 1 =65

But in 5 - 124 → 5³ + 1 = 125 + 1 = 126 ≠ 124

Thus, 5 - 124 is odd one.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the related number form the given alternatives.

110 : 12100 : : 170 : ?
questions.solution:
Pattern here is, second number is the square of the first number i.e.

110 : 12100 → 110² = 12100.

Similarly,

170² = 28900

Therefore 28900 is the correct answer.

Similarly,

9² - 1 = 81 - 1 = 80

Therefore 80 is the correct answer.

questions.question: If 13 L 4 A 7 = 41 and 14 A 3 L 12 = 54, then 12 L 3 A 9 = ?
questions.solution:
Here, L means + and A means × i.e.

13 L 4 A 7 = 13 + 4 × 7 = 13 + 28 = 41

14 A 3 L 12 = 14 × 3 + 12 = 42 + 12 = 54

Similarly,

12 L 3 A 9 = 12 + 3 × 9 = 12 + 27 = 39

Hence, 39 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some white are yellow.

II. All yellow are blue.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some blue are white.

II. Some yellow are white.
questions.solution:
Consider the following least possible Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2fe4a710e4613726203cf70751ec07607fd15bf92d7485ccd466bb74d95f66e2.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some blue are white → True.

II. Some yellow are white → True.

Hence, both I and II follows.

questions.question:
In the following question, some statements followed by some conclusions are given. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which one of the given conclusions logically follows the statements.

**Statements: **

I. All ears are hands.

II. No hand is nose.

**Conclusions:**

I. No ear is nose.

II. All noses are ears.

III. Some hands are noses.
questions.solution:
Consider the following least possible Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e80d23ef066bf52f99aff20205cc82d8875312577ff996f972eec8647e0110cc.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. No ear is nose → True. (definite true as all ears are hands and no hand is nose)

II. All noses are ears → False. (definite false as all ears are hands and no hand is nose)

III. Some hands are noses → False. (definite false as no hand is nose)

Hence, only I follows.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "RUN" is written as "50" and "BUS" is written as "39". How is "GUN" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
Here, if A is 1, B is 2, C is 3 and so on Z will be 26.

The code used here is three less than the sum of the numbers which comes in place of each letter i.e.

RUN → R = 18, U = 21, N = 14 → (18 + 21 + 14) - 3 = 53 - 3 = 50.

BUS → B = 2, U = 21, S = 19 → (2 + 21 + 19) - 3 = 42 - 3 = 39.

Similarly,

GUN → G = 7, U = 21, N = 14 → (7 + 21 + 14) - 3 = 42 - 3 = 39.

questions.question: A is 2 years older to B. B is 5 years younger to C. C is 3 years older to D. D is 6 years younger to E. Who is the youngest?
questions.solution:
According to the question the relation between the ages of A, B, C, D and E are

A = B + 2

B = C - 5

C = D + 3

D = E - 6

Let the age of E be 10 years

D = 10 - 6 = 4 years

C = D + 3 = 4 + 3 = 7 years

B = C - 5 = 7 - 5 = 2 years

A = B + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4 years

Hence, B is the youngest.

questions.question: Weight of P is twice that of Q. Weight of Q is half of R. Weight of R is 3 times of T. Weight of T is half of S. The weight of Q is greater than the weight of how many persons among P, R, S and T?
questions.solution:
According to the questions the relation between the weights of P, Q, R, S, and T are

begin{array}{l} P = 2Q\ Q = (1)/(2)R\ R = 3T\ T = (1)/(2)S to S = 2T end{array}

Let the weight of T be 10kg

S = 2T = 20kg

R = 3T = 30kg

Q = (1)/(2)R = (1)/(2) times 30 = 15kg

P = 2Q = 2 × 15 = 30 kg

Therefore, the weight of Q is greater than T only.
